## Active

### D-513 — The runbook declares the suite it deploys, which is the tenant's act

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · active_

D-507 keeps the declaration out of every kustomization because which suite a namespace runs is the
tenant's decision. A runbook is that tenant for the cluster it owns, so it applies
`example/blongdeployment.yaml` after the tree instead of rendering it for somebody else to apply:
without that step the operator reconciles whatever declaration an earlier run left, which is how a
switched-off service survived a full cycle. Leaving the apply to a developer would make every green
report depend on a step outside the run. Reconsider if a runbook is ever pointed at a cluster whose
tenants are not the run.

### D-641 — The runbook names the suite scenario and artifact

> _2026-10-27 · test/blong-int-kustomize · active_

The machine half of the k3d runbook deploys the suite and operator scenarios by literal name and
publishes suite.zip, so a second deployable package cannot use it without copying it. The scenario,
the archive name and the in-cluster URL are options (SUITE_SCENARIO, ARTIFACT_NAME, and the existing
SUITE_PACKAGE and SUITE_ENTRY), defaulting to suite and suite.zip so the blong-suite cycle is
unchanged. The operator scenario stays fixed: there is one operator per cluster.

### D-952 — A deployment carries no test seed; the runbook makes its own login

> _2026-11-21 · test/blong-int-kustomize · active_

The runbook used to be handed `BLONG_TEST_USER`/`BLONG_TEST_PASSWORD`, which made the check it does
last — a login round trip that proves a released process reached its credential tables — depend on a
test seed being in the deployment. That is wrong in the one place it matters: the suite this runbook
deploys is reachable from the internet, and `testAdmin`/`testPassword` is the administrative UI with
the lock left open. A deployment's database is not a test fixture.

So the run makes its own login. `provisionUser` mints a name nobody would guess and a password from
the CSPRNG that is never written down, grants it `Admin` so the round trip exercises the same
authorization a person meets, and `retireUser` removes it in a `finally` through
`blong-dev user remove` — the verb the tool grew for this, and the counterpart of the `add` it
already had. What a failed run could leave behind is a login nobody holds the password to, in a
database the caller of this runbook already administers.

The connection is the deployment's own, and that is the second half of the decision: an earlier
draft read `.blong_devrc`, which is true on a developer's machine and false on a CI runner — and the
database is not published outside the k3d cluster there either. So the run reads the rc document the
tree mounts into every pod (`blong-releaserc-etc`), follows the ExternalName the suite dials (`db` →
`mysql.blong-integration`), port-forwards that Service on 13306 and hands the coordinates to
`blong-dev user`. Nothing is named in a workflow, in `deploy.sh` or in the machine's rc.

`BLONG_TEST_USER` still wins when a caller sets it, because a caller with a seed and a reason for it
should not be second-guessed; nothing in this repository sets it any more.
